ISS-oracle-ipv6-ssrf.title: SSRF guard misses bracketed IPv6 literals
ISS-oracle-ipv6-ssrf.summary: validateSourceURL/hostBlocked fails to recognize bracketed IPv6 URL hosts: net.ParseIP("[::1]") is nil (brackets not accepted), so [::1], [fc00::1], [fe80::1] fall through to DNS lookup, which fails -> reported NOT blocked on every host. All IPv6-literal SSRF vectors bypass the guard.

ISS-http-probe-panic.title: http loopback probe panics instead of skipping

Contradicts decision-http-tests-env-skip (just test green on this host).

ISS-084.title: Phantom on-chain blocks on rolled-back transactions: token Mint/Transfer/TransferFrom/Burn, NFT Transfer/Burn, voting CastVote and lottery all call chain.AddBlock BEFORE the domain transaction commits; a lost race (double-spend/ownership-changed/already-voted) rolls the tx back but the block persists, violating the chain invariant that every block = a committed operation. Voting documents it as an accepted best-effort tradeoff (its vote-row needs the height before save). Deferred: see DEC-002.

DEC-002.rationale: Best-effort on-chain audit blocks are accepted for now: block height must exist before the domain row save (audit records carry it), and the chain is a separate DB + in-memory singleton that a domain DB rollback cannot undo, so atomicity needs a cross-DB redesign. The token EVENT trail is already hardened (events publish only after commit, v1.68 / ISS-074) and a pre-tx race merely leaves a best-effort audit block, never corrupts committed balances. Revisit when a block-height reservation or after-commit height backfill design lands.
DEC-002.alternatives_rejected: Moving AddBlock post-commit for token only changes block ordering and is inconsistent across subsystems

DEC-003.rationale: Embedding the API key in served HTML (injectKeyIntoHTML) is accepted for the single-user local dev UI: the browser needs the key to call the API same-origin, and the design compensates by refusing wildcard CORS (v1.64 / TASK-077) and by the rate limiter + body cap bounding the blast radius. A production-ish hardening (short-lived session tokens, CSRF) is documented in webauth.go as future work.
DEC-003.alternatives_rejected: Removing the key from served HTML and requiring an operator-entered session token changes the UX surface and is out of scope for the dev-first product

ISS-111.title: Failed post-commit audit publish is reported but never healed (no retry/queue/idempotency)
ISS-111.summary:
v1.82 TASK-117/CHG-111 correctly reports ErrAuditPublishFailed so a committed op is never presented as failed (CLI do-not-retry warning + API AUDIT_PUBLISH_FAILED code), but nothing heals the loss: SyncEventBus.Publish fan-out is synchronous, the only durability is the audit handler's SQLite INSERT at delivery time, and on failure the event is dropped with no trace. There is no outbox table, no failed-event store, no retry loop, no DEAD queue, no dedup/idempotency column. Committed domain state stands and the audit record is permanently lost. IS
S-084 (phantom blocks) is parked, but this is the audit-loss side of the same post-commit gap and is addressable without a cross-DB atomicity redesign: a durable pending-outbox that is drained by a retry loop, with the events table PK (random UUID) making INSERT OR IGNORE / ON CONFLICT idempotent.

Also untested: multi-DB restore partial failure, DatabaseChecksums path through Restore verify, .pre_restore restorability after a mid-restore failure, symlink alias guard.

TASK-119.title: Build a durable post-commit retry/queue for failed audit publishes

Must be idempotent (events PK is a random UUID => INSERT OR IGNORE / ON CONFLICT). Keep scope tight: retry loop with backoff, failed-store or status column, CLI/API unchanged (still authoritative about commit).

TASK-120.title: Backup restore hardening + real-binary exerciser under a live WAL-writing server
TASK-120.summary: Fold the backup deep-dive (round 95) correctness findings into one hardening + exerciser effort: (1) add an e2e/CLI test running backup restore through the real path against a live WAL-writing server asserting the restored DB holds the latest committed data; (2) close restore gaps found in the deep-dive — restore is NOT atomic across DBs (DB N failure leaves DBs 0..N-1 replaced, per-DB alias guard can fire mid-loop), Create's metadata.json write is not atomic (crash → truncated metadata over new .db files; checksum failure post-promote yields inconsistent set), TOCTOU between Verify and Restore's copy, hardcoded 0640 perms/ownership replacing a group-shared live DB, restore destination has no temp+rename (mid-copy disk-full leaves truncated .db), legacy-archive verify only checks table-presence (corrupt-but-parseable archive can overwrite good DB). Define WAL/commit semantics explicitly.

DEC-007.rationale: The web UI is served by cmd/api (a local tool that should work offline). Loading Alpine from the unpkg CDN (a) adds a third-party supply-chain/interception surface between the operator and their data, (b) breaks the UI when the machine is offline or unpkg is unreachable, and (c) cannot be integrity-verified at every load without SRI. SRI-on-CDN hardens (c) but not (a)/(b). Vendoring the verified alpinejs@3.13.5 build (byte-checked against its published SRI base64) into web/vendor/alpine.min.js removes the external dependency entirely — a one-time ~44KiB asset matching the repo's self-contained ethos.
DEC-007.alternatives_rejected: SRI-integrity attribute on the CDN script tag: still requires network and leaves a live third-party dependency/availability risk. CSP with unpkg allow-list: same availability coupling. No change: leaves the supply-chain + offline-break risk open.

ISS-242.title: Multi-process writes to a shared chain DB silently overwrite committed blocks: appendBlock derives height := int64(len(c.Blocks)) from the process-local in-memory slice (block.go:116) and the persist callback is INSERT OR REPLACE keyed on that height (init.go). Two processes sharing ./data/aurora.db (documented norms: the API server + a CLI lottery/oracle command), each boots genesis into a 1-element chain, so both compute height 1 for their first post-reload append and REPLACE the same row — the loser payload is silently lost; in-memory chains then diverge (each appends height 2 with its own PrevHash), and the next restart fails VerifyIntegrity. Not merely dropped: the tampered ledger line surfaces as persistent corruption detected only by chain-hash verification. Fix needs a height-reservation / DB-authoritative-height design (revisit DEC-002); registered as a design task. Source: internal/domain/blockchain/block.go:103-151 + init.go persist (verified read)

DEC-011.title: Multi-process height reservation is DB-authoritative via plain-INSERT UNIQUE conflict + bounded drop-and-retry (resolves ISS-242, closes TASK-244)
DEC-011.rationale: The in-process write lock in appendBlock only serializes callers within one process; two processes sharing a-db each compute height from their process-local len(Blocks), so both can reserve height N and the old INSERT OR REPLACE silently dropped the loser's committed row. Heights must be assigned by the DB, not the local slice. Implemented: persist writes a plain INSERT and maps the height PRIMARY-KEY UNIQUE violation to ErrHeightConflict; appendBlock re-syncs the in-memory chain from the shared DB (syncFromDB, folds rows at height>=tail) before reserving, and on ErrHeightConflict drops its losing candidate and retries at the true next free height (bounded at 5 attempts). This makes a committed block immutable on disk and both processes' payloads survive at distinct heights; audit records re-stamped with the final height. Persisting under the write lock (rather than after unlock) is what makes drop-on-conflict safe — no other local caller can interleave.
alternatives_rejected: INSERT OR REPLACE (the bug: silently lossy)
separate reservation table / sequence (overkill: height PK provides the atomic UNIQUE guard)
give up on multi-process appends and require a lock file (rejects a documented operating norm)

DEC-016.rationale: Re-examined ISS-084 against the round 144-146 DB-authoritative height reservation (TASK-244, ISS-242): that work makes heights conflict-free across processes (syncFromDB + ErrHeightConflict retry + phantom-tail rebuild) but does NOT address the domain-rollback coupling — the token/NFT/voting/lottery services still call AddBlock before the domain SQLite tx commits, so a losing side of a race (double-spend / already-voted / ownership-changed) leaves a committed on-chain block for a rolled-back op. Voting genuinely needs the block height before its vote-row save, so a blanket post-commit AddBlock is impossible (DEC-002 rejected it). The viable forward path is a reserve-then-finalize protocol (mark a block pending, finalize only on domain commit, reclaim on rollback) — a deliberate cross-subsystem design effort for a dedicated round, not a hasty patch. Tradeoff remains accepted per DEC-002; issue stays active.
DEC-016.alternatives_rejected: Move AddBlock post-commit for token/nft (changes block ordering, impossible for voting, inconsistent across subsystems — DEC-002); leave ISS-084 unexamined after the round 144-146 change (risk a future loop misreading the height work as having closed it)

DEC-018.title: Allowance expires_at stays write-only-documented; expiry enforcement deferred (not a defect, aligned with DEC-002)
DEC-018.rationale: Round-145 Go audit Finding 4: the allowances table carries an expires_at column and ApproveEvent/Approval expose it, but nothing ever sets a non-zero value (TryAdjustApproval inserts 0 = never) and TransferFrom never consults it. Every allowance in the system is therefore live forever, so no current input produces wrong money behavior — expiry is a documented-but-unimplemented knob, not a funds bug. Options were: (a) enforce expiry in TransferFrom + approval reads, or (b) drop the column/accessors. Enforcement adds a real feature (expiring allowances) that no surface exposes and changes DEC-002 allowance semantics; dropping the column breaks the ApproveEvent API and the shipped schema for no behavior gain. Both are product decisions beyond a polish round and carry migration risk (a schema change on a stored DB with allowance rows). Deferred: record the knobs unimplemented status here so a future round treats it as a decision, not a latent bug.
DEC-018.alternatives_rejected: Implement expiry enforcement now (feature scope creep, no surface requests it, changes signed Allowance semantics); drop the expires_at column/accessors (approval API break + schema migration on stored data for zero runtime gain)

DEC-019.title: CSP is stripped on the aurora:// transport; the HTTP gateway keeps its strict nonce policy

So the transport, not the policy, is made responsible for the custom-scheme window: stripCSP wraps only Runtime.Handler, and reachability is bounded by the scheme handler serving just the embedded files with no listener and no remote origin.

ISS-333.title: Desktop database backups are readable by other local users
ISS-333.description: The desktop File > Backup action snapshots the SQLite database into a timestamped directory chosen by the user. BackupService.Create uses MkdirAll(output, 0755), lets VACUUM INTO create the database with the process umask (0644 under the default 022), and writes metadata.json as 0640. The database stores operator-supplied Oracle request headers, which may contain bearer tokens, so another local account can read a backup even though the live desktop data tree is now owner-only.

TASK-339.outcome: New backup sets are 0700 and SQLite snapshots plus metadata are 0600; an existing output directory keeps its own mode but new files remain owner-only. The red test observed 0755/0644 under umask 022, then passed at 0700/0600 after the fix; the backup package, desktop checks and desktop race suite are green.

TASK-340.title: Make on-chain audit blocks atomic with domain SQLite transactions
TASK-340.description: Use the shared aurora.db transaction to insert each block together with token/NFT/voting/lottery/oracle state. Add a transaction-aware BlockChain write API that mines under the chain lock, inserts through the domain *sql.Tx, appends to memory only after commit, and retries height conflicts. Refactor every pre-transaction AddBlock/AddLotteryRecord caller and prove rollback leaves neither a database row nor an in-memory block. Replace the obsolete cross-DB deferral in DEC-002.
TASK-340.outcome: Blocks and domain rows now commit or roll back together for token, NFT, voting, lottery, and Oracle over the shared aurora.db. The chain holds its lock through commit, appends to memory only after success, and retries height conflicts before any business callback. Real-SQLite rollback tests are green; fault-injecting the old ordering made all five regressions red with a phantom in-memory block. Full CGO_ENABLED=0 tests, relevant race tests, golangci-lint, desktop-check, desktop-race, and build-current passed.

ISS-334.title: Concurrent SQLite migrators observe transient dirty state or both pass the version check
ISS-334.description: TestMigrator_ConcurrentOpenersSerialize fails deterministically with migration up failed: database is dirty at version 1 (go test -count=20 ./internal/infra/migrate -run TestMigrator_ConcurrentOpenersSerialize). Migrator.up reads schema_migrations before opening a write transaction, then run() marks dirty, applies SQL and clears dirty in three separate transactions. A peer can therefore read the transient dirty marker and fail even though the migration is succeeding; two peers that both read the same clean version can also enter the same migration before either marks it dirty. BEGIN IMMEDIATE and busy_timeout only serialize transactions, not this read/check/run gap.

TASK-341.title: Serialize migration version checks with the migration transaction
TASK-341.description: Hold one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction across the dirty check and every migration step so concurrent openers wait, then re-read the committed version and skip work already applied by the winner. Preserve crash-safety: a failed SQL body rolls back only that migration through a savepoint, leaves the target version dirty, and returns the original failure. Cover concurrent up/down and the existing failed-migration dirty contract without weakening assertions.

CHG-340.title: Commit business rows and on-chain audit blocks in one SQLite transaction; insert under the chain lock, append memory after commit, retry height conflicts, and cover token/NFT/voting/lottery/Oracle rollback with real SQLite tests (ISS-084)

DEC-033.title: Place audit blocks and domain rows in one shared-SQLite transaction
DEC-033.rationale: Token, NFT, voting, lottery and Oracle already share aurora.db. The chain now exposes a transaction-aware append API that inserts the proof-of-work block through the caller's *sql.Tx, runs the domain mutation before commit, and appends to the in-memory chain only after commit. The chain lock spans height reservation through commit so concurrent writers cannot mine against an uncommitted predecessor; lock ordering is chain then SQLite. Height conflicts remain DB-authoritative and retry before the business callback, so failed attempts have no domain side effects. Tests prove rollback removes both the block row and in-memory block across all five subsystems.
DEC-033.alternatives_rejected: Cross-DB block reservation plus after-commit height backfill; appending the block only after commit while leaving the business row without its audit height; relying on compensation or background reconciliation instead of one transaction

ISS-343.title: Oracle SSRF validation still has a DNS rebinding window: ValidateSourceURL resolves the source hostname before the request, but net/http resolves it again at dial time; an attacker-controlled DNS answer can be public during validation and private for the actual connection, and the same gap exists when checkRedirectAllowed resolves a redirect target
ISS-343.description: The v1.54 fetch-time revalidation (CHG-065) narrows but does not close ISS-059. It performs one resolver lookup, then http.Client performs another. securityTransport previously delegated to http.DefaultTransport without checking the concrete resolved IP, so a rebinding response could reach loopback, RFC1918, link-local/cloud metadata, or other blocked space. The redirected-request policy has the same validation/dial gap because its lookup is not pinned either. Fix belongs at net.Dialer.ControlContext, where the exact IP about to be connected is available.

TASK-350.title: Enforce the oracle SSRF private-address policy on the concrete IP net/http dials
TASK-350.description: Install a net.Dialer.ControlContext on the oracle fetcher transport that rejects blocked IPs immediately before connect, preserving the standard transport behavior and redirect policy. Add direct policy tests for IPv4/IPv6 blocked and public addresses plus a regression that the default Fetcher transport attaches the guard; keep httptest loopback tests on an explicit test-only unguarded transport.

CHG-349.title: Guard the concrete oracle dial address and close custom TLS-dial bypasses (TASK-350, ISS-343)
CHG-349.description: Added a ControlContext destination check to every Fetcher transport, including IPv4/IPv6 loopback, private, link-local and unresolved addresses. The transport now clears custom TLS dial hooks so HTTPS cannot bypass DialContext, tracks the actual proxy selection per request so only operator-configured proxy endpoints are exempt, and keeps test-only loopback fetchers behind an explicit helper. Fault injection first failed with the sandbox socket error rather than ErrBlockedDestination; the new regression then passed. Oracle HTTP shuffle/count=20, full non-migration shuffle/count=5, vet, desktop-check, check and build-current all pass.

TASK-354.title: Keep CLI/API log directories and files owner-only, including pre-existing loose paths
TASK-354.description: Create log directories as 0700, create aurora.log as 0600, and chmod existing paths during logger.Init so a prior umask or version cannot preserve exposure. Add a Unix regression that pre-creates loose paths and one that creates them under umask 022; both must fail before the permissions change.

CHG-353.title: Keep logger directories and files owner-only and repair loose modes
CHG-353.description: logger.Init now creates log directories as 0700, opens aurora.log as 0600, chmods existing paths, skips Unix chmod on Windows, and falls back to console if hardening fails. Unix regressions cover fresh and pre-existing loose paths.

ISS-348.title: CLI initializes logging before Cobra loads config, so the empty level disables every log and the configured log path and level are ignored
ISS-348.description: Evidence: an isolated `aurora version` run under umask 022 emitted no structured log and created no logs directory. cmd/aurora/main.go calls logger.Init before rootCmd.Execute, but [log] defaults and the config file are loaded by Cobra initConfig during Execute. zerolog.ParseLevel("") returns NoLevel without an error, so the early logger suppresses Info and later calls never reinitialize it with the loaded path.

TASK-355.title: Initialize CLI file logging after config loading and treat an empty level as info
TASK-355.description: Move the operational startup log behind config initialization, reinitialize the logger from the loaded [log] settings before command execution, and make logger.Init default an empty level to info. Add an end-to-end CLI regression with an alternate --config log path; it must produce the startup record in that file and fail against the old initialization order.

CHG-354.title: Apply CLI logging config before command execution and default empty levels to info
CHG-354.description: Cobra now reinitializes the logger from [log] in PersistentPreRunE and emits the startup record only after config loading. logger.Init maps an empty level to info instead of zerolog NoLevel. A real root-command regression verifies the alternate config path receives the startup record, and CLI test logging is isolated to temp paths.

ISS-349.title: CLI silently ignores malformed or explicitly missing config files and runs against defaults
ISS-349.description: Evidence: `aurora --config <malformed.toml> version` exits 0, prints normal version output and creates the default ./logs path with no warning. cmd/aurora/cmd/root.go calls viper.ReadInConfig but only checks err == nil, swallowing syntax errors and missing explicit files just like the benign no-config-found search result. Dangerous commands can therefore operate on the default database after the operator supplied an invalid config.

TASK-356.title: Fail CLI startup on malformed or explicitly missing config files while allowing optional search absence
TASK-356.description: Capture viper.ReadInConfig errors, tolerate only ConfigFileNotFoundError during default path search, and return every other error from PersistentPreRunE before initializing logging or running a command. Add root-command regressions for malformed content and an explicit missing --config path; both must fail before the production change.

CHG-355.title: Reject malformed or explicitly missing CLI config before command execution
CHG-355.description: CLI initConfig now records every ReadInConfig error except ConfigFileNotFoundError during the optional $HOME/cwd search. PersistentPreRunE returns that error before logging initialization or command work. Regressions cover malformed TOML and an explicitly missing --config path.

ISS-350.title: Logger console fallback writes structured logs to stdout, contaminating CLI output and duplicating errors
ISS-350.description: Observed while rejecting malformed config: the friendly error goes to stderr, but logger.Error also prints a console-formatted Application error record to stdout. Any script consuming CLI stdout receives a non-result line, and docs promise failures use one stderr line. The same fallback applies when a configured log file cannot be opened.

TASK-357.title: Route console fallback logs to stderr so CLI stdout remains machine-readable
TASK-357.description: Change the zerolog ConsoleWriter fallback from stdout to stderr and add a regression that captures both streams around logger.Init plus a log event. Verify command errors leave stdout empty while stderr retains the structured diagnostic and friendly error line.

ISS-351.title: Restore can report failure after replacing the live database and commits multiple databases one at a time, leaving a partially restored multi-store state
ISS-351.description: internal/infra/backup/backup.go:473-559 restores each configured DB inside one map loop. Alias/pre-restore/copy errors for a later DB return after earlier destinations were renamed; even a single DB can commit os.Rename then return an error from the -wal/-shm cleanup. A caller sees failure although live data changed. TASK-120 documented multi-DB atomicity but closed with only per-file temp+rename.

TASK-358.title: Make BackupService.Restore all-or-nothing across configured databases and post-promotion failures
TASK-358.description: Preflight every configured database name, alias, destination shape, and backup copy before touching live files; prepare every replacement temp and WAL-complete pre-restore snapshot first; then promote in deterministic order. If any promotion or stale-WAL cleanup fails, roll back every already-promoted database from its pre-restore snapshot and remove destinations that did not previously exist. Add a regression that injects a post-promotion -wal cleanup failure and proves the original live DB is restored while Restore returns the failure.

DEC-034.title: Stage and roll back every BackupService.Restore database instead of committing them one at a time
DEC-034.rationale: Separate databases on arbitrary filesystems cannot share one atomic filesystem transaction. Full preflight plus staged snapshots/replacements removes all known preparation and alias failures from the commit window. Deterministic promotion and rollback from WAL-complete pre-restore snapshots make post-promotion failures recoverable and testable. The refactor exceeds the normal 300-line advisory because it replaces the embedded per-DB loop with explicit plan, prepare, promote, and rollback phases.
DEC-034.alternatives_rejected: Keep per-file temp+rename and document that a failed multi-DB restore may be partial; attach every SQLite database to one transaction (not portable across separate filesystems configured paths and does not handle arbitrary files); rely on the operator manually recovering earlier databases from .pre_restore after an error.

CHG-357.title: Atomic staged rollback for multi-database backup restore
CHG-357.summary: BackupService.Restore now requires archive/configuration database sets to match, preflights all aliases and destination shapes, prepares every WAL-complete pre-restore snapshot and replacement temp before touching a live DB, promotes in sorted order, and rolls back all promoted files on a later failure. Fault injection added for post-promotion WAL cleanup; the multi-DB alias regression reproduced the old partial restore on attempt 0 and is now green.

ISS-352.title: The pinned golangci-lint v2.15.0 CI gate fails with three SA1019 warnings because the SSRF transport intentionally references deprecated Transport.DialTLS to neutralize it
ISS-352.description: go run with golangci-lint v2.15.0 on Go 1.27.2 reports SA1019 for internal/infra/http/fetcher.go:371 and fetcher_dial_guard_test.go:129,138. CI runs the same version with errcheck disabled, so these are the only remaining mandatory lint failures. The production reference is intentional: a cloned embedding transport may carry the deprecated DialTLS hook, which would bypass the guarded DialContext for direct HTTPS.

TASK-359.title: Keep the intentional deprecated TLS-hook neutralization while restoring the pinned lint gate
TASK-359.description: Add narrowly scoped staticcheck suppressions that explain why DialTLS must be cleared for security and why the regression test constructs it. Do not remove the DialTLS clearing or weaken the dial guard. Verify the full CI lint command (golangci-lint v2.15.0, errcheck disabled) exits clean, then rerun the fetcher tests and full non-migrate test suite.

CHG-358.title: Lint-clean intentional TLS dial-hook neutralization
CHG-358.summary: Added targeted staticcheck explanations at the production DialTLS clear and the two deprecated-field references in the SSRF regression test. The guard behavior is unchanged; golangci-lint v2.15.0 with errcheck disabled now reports 0 issues, matching the CI command.

ISS-353.title: The protected Oracle fetch endpoint discards the HTTP request context, so client disconnects and server shutdown cannot cancel the outbound fetch
ISS-353.description: internal/api/handler/oracle.go:208-213 constructs the use case and calls Execute, which hardcodes context.Background in internal/app/oracle/usecase.go:75-77. The scheduler already calls ExecuteContext, but REST fetch does not. A disconnected client leaves the upstream request running until the fetcher timeout (10s default), consuming a handler goroutine, rate-limit budget, and outbound connection; request cancellation is observable in r.Context().

TASK-360.title: Propagate the REST request context into Oracle FetchDataUseCase
TASK-360.description: Call ExecuteContext(r.Context()) from OracleHandler.Fetch and add a cancellation regression with a context-aware fetcher that blocks until the request is canceled. Keep the existing shared-fetcher and scheduler behavior unchanged, then run handler/API tests, race tests, vet, lint, and build.

CHG-359.title: Propagate request cancellation through Oracle REST fetch
CHG-359.summary: OracleHandler.Fetch now calls FetchDataUseCase.ExecuteContext(r.Context()) instead of the background-context Execute wrapper. A blocking context-aware fetcher regression proved the old path ignored cancellation and now observes it immediately. Handler/API package tests and race tests pass.

COMP-021.name: internal/api/server.go
COMP-021.description: HTTP API composition root: NewServer opens the blockchain singleton plus lottery, voting, NFT, token, event, replay, and oracle SQLite handles and wires their handlers; Server.Close owns their release.

ISS-354.title: NewServer leaks every SQLite handle opened before a later dependency fails
ISS-354.description: internal/api/server.go initializes the blockchain singleton and several repositories in sequence, registering successful opens in Server.closers, but every later constructor error returns nil without calling Close. A boot-time schema/open failure therefore strands the global DB and all earlier repository/event/replay handles until process exit. Source: NewServer error returns at server.go and Server.Close ownership contract (verified read).

TASK-361.title: Release every SQLite handle when NewServer initialization fails
TASK-361.description: Made NewServer all-or-nothing: incomplete construction now runs Server.Close so every registered repository/event/replay handle and the blockchain singleton are released. The regression forces voting setup to fail after lottery opens via a pre-existing incompatible votes table, asserts the blockchain pool is closed, and on Linux checks /proc/self/fd for leaked main/WAL/SHM handles. Fault injections proved both total and partial cleanup regressions turn it red.

HYP-049.title: NewServer direct error returns leave every SQLite handle opened before the failing constructor live
HYP-049.description: The constructor registers successful repositories in Server.closers, but direct error returns bypass Close. A deterministic voting schema failure after the blockchain and lottery opens should therefore leave both DB pools live; routing every incomplete construction through Server.Close should release all handles.

EV-145.source: internal/api/server_cleanup_test.go; 2026-10-24 fault injections: removing cleanup defer made db.Ping succeed after NewServer error; replacing Server.Close with blockchain.Close made /proc/self/fd show the lottery pool plus aurora.db/WAL/SHM; final go test ./internal/api -shuffle=on -count=20, -race -count=3, and go test ./... -cover all green
EV-145.title: A mid-construction failure is deterministic and the regression detects both total and partial handle leaks

CHG-360.title: Route incomplete API server construction through Server.Close
CHG-360.description: Adds an all-or-nothing completion flag and deferred Server.Close on every pre-success return, plus a schema-conflict regression that checks the blockchain pool is closed and Linux /proc file descriptors contain no leaked repository/WAL/SHM handles.

ISS-355.title: Backup Create can replace the previous database set and then fail before publishing matching metadata
ISS-355.description: internal/infra/backup/backup.go Create snapshots every DB to temp and then promotes each snapshot over the existing backup before checksumming/writing metadata. A checksum, metadata write, metadata rename, or output walk failure after promotion returns an error while the previous good .db set is already gone and the old metadata.json no longer matches it. The existing MetadataWriteError test asserts only that Create errors, not that the previous verifiable set survives. Source: Create phase 2 through metadata tail (verified read).

TASK-362.title: Roll back Create after any snapshot promotion or metadata-tail failure
TASK-362.description: Make BackupService.Create transactional over an existing output directory: preflight names and metadata paths, retain a private rollback copy of every pre-existing DB and metadata file before promotion, restore that exact set if any promotion/checksum/metadata/walk step fails, and remove files newly created by the failed run. Add deterministic regressions for a post-promotion metadata temp collision and an injected mid-promotion rename failure; both must leave the previous backup byte-identical and Verify-green.

DEC-035.title: Stage every previous BackupService.Create output and roll it back before publishing a new set
DEC-035.rationale: Create cannot atomically replace multiple database files plus metadata with one rename. Before promotion, validate configured names and path shapes, then hard-link every existing database and metadata file into a private same-filesystem rollback directory (falling back to an atomic copy). On any promotion, checksum, metadata, or output-walk failure, restore promoted files in reverse order, remove outputs that did not previously exist, and discard the rollback directory only when every restore succeeds. Retaining that directory after a rollback failure preserves the prior data for operator recovery. The refactor exceeds the 300-line advisory because it adds transactional staging and three fault-injected regressions.
DEC-035.alternatives_rejected: Roll back only metadata (leaves newly promoted databases under old metadata); replace the whole output directory atomically (no portable multi-file exchange and would delete unrelated files); leave the new database set and return an error (creates an unverifiable mixed set); delete rollback artifacts even when restoring a previous file fails (discards the only retained recovery copy).

HYP-050.title: Replacing every previous backup database before the metadata tail leaves failed Create calls with no consistent restorable set
HYP-050.description: BackupService.Create promotes each new database snapshot by rename, then computes checksums, writes metadata, promotes metadata, and walks the output. Before this change, any error in that tail returned after the old database files and metadata were already unrecoverable, leaving new databases beside old or absent metadata. Staging the complete previous visible set before promotion and restoring it on every tail failure should make Create all-or-nothing.

EV-146.title: Fault-injected promotion, metadata, and first-create failures all preserve or clean the backup set
EV-146.source: internal/infra/backup/backup_test.go:360 TestBackupService_Create_MetadataFailureRollsBackPreviousSet, :397 TestBackupService_Create_NewOutputCleansUpAfterMetadataFailure, :421 TestBackupService_Create_PromotionFailureRollsBackPreviousSet; 2026-10-24 fault injection: removing rollbackCreate made both previous-set tests fail on changed database hashes; final go test ./internal/infra/backup -shuffle=on -count=20, CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race ./internal/infra/backup -shuffle=on -count=3, go test ./... -cover, just check, just desktop-check, and golangci-lint v2.15.0 all green

CHG-361.title: Make BackupService.Create transactional over existing output directories
CHG-361.description: Validate configured names, stage the previous databases and metadata in a private same-filesystem rollback directory, promote in deterministic order, and restore the previous set or remove newly created outputs after any promotion, checksum, metadata, or walk failure. Add regressions for the first create, a post-promotion metadata blocker, and an injected mid-promotion failure.

ISS-356.title: Backup Verify/Restore follow database symlinks outside the archive and Create writes metadata through a symlinked temp file
ISS-356.description: internal/infra/backup/backup.go uses os.Stat for archive <name>.db in Verify and planRestore, so a symlink inside an operator-supplied backup directory is accepted as a regular database and its target is hashed/opened/copied during restore. Create also writes metadata.json.tmp in the caller-controlled output directory with os.WriteFile, which follows a planted symlink and can overwrite an arbitrary target before renaming the symlink itself to metadata.json. Source: Verify database stat/open loop, planRestore backup stat, and Create metadata-tail write (verified read).

TASK-363.title: Reject symlinked backup artifacts and keep Create metadata staging private
TASK-363.description: Require archive database and metadata files to be regular directory entries rather than symlinks; restore must refuse an external symlink before touching live data. Move Create metadata staging into the private same-filesystem rollback directory, remove stale caller-controlled metadata temp entries safely, and inject metadata-write failure so post-promotion rollback stays deterministic. Add regressions for an external database symlink and a symlinked metadata temp that must not modify its target.

DEC-036.title: Treat backup archive files as regular directory entries and stage Create metadata only inside the private rollback directory
DEC-036.rationale: Archive database and metadata paths are attacker-influenced. Following a symlink makes Verify or Restore read, hash, or copy a file outside the supplied archive, while a planted metadata.json.tmp symlink made Create overwrite an arbitrary host file before renaming the link to metadata.json. Lstat regular-file checks reject link directory entries without rejecting legitimate hard-linked regular files. Create now writes and renames metadata from the already-required 0700 same-filesystem rollback directory, so no caller-controlled temp path is opened, and an injectable writer keeps post-promotion failure tests deterministic.
DEC-036.alternatives_rejected: Resolve symlinks and compare path prefixes (still racy and vulnerable to link swaps), rely on database checksums (the target is read before the checksum can reject it), open the public metadata temp with O_NOFOLLOW (non-portable and leaves a writable temp surface), or unlink symlinks during Restore (mutates the operator input instead of refusing a non-self-contained archive).

HYP-051.title: Following backup archive and public temp symlinks lets backup operations escape their declared directory
HYP-051.description: Verify and planRestore treated a symlinked database as a regular archive file because they used os.Stat, so a crafted archive could make verification and restore read or copy an external target. Create wrote metadata.json.tmp in the caller-controlled output directory, so a planted symlink caused os.WriteFile to overwrite its target and could leave metadata.json as that symlink. Lstat-based regular-entry checks plus private metadata staging should close both paths without breaking hard-linked backups.

EV-147.title: Symlink regressions fail on the old Stat/public-temp implementation and pass with private staging
EV-147.source: internal/infra/backup/backup_test.go:418 TestBackupService_Create_DoesNotFollowSymlinkedMetadataTemp, internal/infra/backup/restore_test.go:471 TestVerifyAndRestore_RejectSymlinkedDatabase, :510 TestVerifyAndRestore_RejectSymlinkedMetadata; 2026-10-24 fault injection: restoring os.Stat plus the output metadata temp made the victim file contain metadata JSON and Verify accept an external database symlink; final backup tests -shuffle -count=20, backup race -count=3, go test -race ./..., go test ./... -cover, just check, just desktop-check, and golangci-lint v2.15.0 all green

CHG-362.title: Reject symlinked backup archive files and stage Create metadata privately
CHG-362.description: Require metadata and database archive entries to pass Lstat regular-file checks in Verify, Restore, and planRestore. Move metadata writing into the private rollback directory and safely unlink a stale caller-controlled metadata.json.tmp entry. Inject the metadata writer so rollback tests can still fail after promotion.

HYP-052.title: SQLite persistence drops the lottery VRF public key and trusts imported verification flags
HYP-052.description: The domain record carries VRFPublicKey and the API verifies proofs against it, but the self-bootstrapped SQLite schema, Save statement, and all SELECT scans omit the key. Every read therefore returns an empty key and verification silently downgrades to deterministic winner matching. The portable importer also stores the caller-provided Verified bit without re-verifying the proof.

EV-148.title: All lottery repository paths omit VRFPublicKey
EV-148.description: internal/infra/sqlite/lottery.go:112-123 creates lottery_records without vrf_public_key; Save at :147-162 does not bind record.VRFPublicKey; GetByID/GetAll/GetByBlockHeight at :171-174, :202-205, :243-246 select no key and return records without it. internal/app/lottery/portability.go:138-150 validates and saves imported records without calling VerifyRecord or canonicalizing Verified.
EV-148.source: internal/infra/sqlite/lottery.go:112-276; internal/app/lottery/portability.go:138-150; static read at HEAD e3a6776

ISS-357.title: Lottery VRF evidence is lost in SQLite and import trusts Verified metadata
ISS-357.description: Records created with a VRF public key are stored without it, so history/export/import and post-restart verification lose the cryptographic proof anchor and fall back to deterministic winner matching. Separately, ImportRecords accepts the serialized Verified=true flag without checking the key or proof, allowing a portable document to manufacture a verified audit trail.

TASK-364.title: Persist and re-verify lottery VRF evidence across SQLite and imports
TASK-364.description: Add an idempotent lottery VRF-key side table through both self-bootstrap and migration 000004 so legacy databases upgrade safely. Save the public key and join it into every lottery read. Make ImportRecords reject records whose stored winners/proof/key fail VerifyRecord and canonicalize Verified from the proof result instead of trusting document metadata. Add repository, migration, CLI, app, and desktop round-trip regressions, including a forged Verified fault injection.

DEC-037.title: Persist lottery VRF keys in an idempotent side table and derive import Verified from verification
DEC-037.rationale: lottery_records is created both by self-bootstrapping repositories and by migrations. A column added by ALTER TABLE in 000004 would fail with duplicate-column if the updated repository bootstrapped first; checking table_info in plain SQL is not portable in the migration runner. lottery_vrf_keys uses CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS in both paths, mirrors the vote_sessions upgrade precedent, and keeps the proof key atomic with Save inside a transaction. ImportRecords must run the same VerifyRecord used by CLI/API/desktop, reject inconsistent records, and derive Verified from ProofVerified so JSON metadata cannot manufacture an audit claim.
DEC-037.alternatives_rejected: Adding vrf_public_key to 000001 mutates an already-applied migration and cannot upgrade existing databases. ALTER TABLE in 000004 plus a self-bootstrap ALTER makes migration order non-idempotent. Trusting the imported Verified boolean permits forged verification metadata. Rejecting every keyless legacy record would break backward-compatible imports, so keyless records remain importable but unverified.

DEC-038.title: Keep lottery storage and import evidence hardening in one commit despite the test-heavy diff
DEC-038.rationale: The change is one audit-integrity invariant exercised at both boundaries: a key must survive SQLite/export and an importer must not trust metadata. The apparent diff exceeds the usual 300-line soft limit because multiple existing desktop/CLI fixtures fabricated unverifiable VRF proofs and had to be replaced with real signed draws. Splitting the commits would leave fake or untrusted-evidence fixtures inconsistent with one half of the invariant and make either commit fail its own end-to-end tests. The production-code delta is small; most added lines are regression coverage and migration-version updates.
DEC-038.alternatives_rejected: Splitting into persistence and import commits would create an intermediate revision whose shared export/import tests cannot all pass without temporary fixture churn. Reducing coverage or preserving fabricated-proof fixtures would hide the exact regression this task fixes.

EV-149.title: Lottery VRF evidence survives SQLite, migration, export/import and forged metadata tests
EV-149.description: Commit 917b8b5 adds the key side table and migration 000004, joins the key into all read paths, verifies imports, and derives Verified from ProofVerified. Fault injection removing the key upsert made TestLotteryRepository_Save_AndGetByID, TestLotteryRepository_VRFPublicKeyOnEveryReadPath, and TestLotteryRepository_UpgradesLegacySchemaWithVRFKeyTable fail with an empty key. Removing the import verifier made TestImportRecords_DoesNotTrustVerifiedWithoutAKey and TestImportRecords_RejectsAnInvalidKeyedProof fail. Restoration passed focused tests, full go test ./..., full race, coverage, just check, just desktop-check, and golangci-lint with 0 issues.

CHG-363.title: Persist lottery VRF keys and re-verify imported evidence
CHG-363.description: Adds lottery_vrf_keys through repository self-bootstrap and migration 000004, writes it transactionally with every draw, joins it into ID/history/height reads, clears it on reset, and rejects or canonicalizes imported records through VerifyRecord. Updates CLI/desktop fixtures to use real signed draws and migration tests through version 4.

HYP-053.title: A VRF-valid lottery draw can report tampered or missing winner addresses as verified
HYP-053.description: DrawWinners derives each winner address as NameToAddress(winner), but VerifyRecord only warns when the address slice length differs and never compares same-length address values. VerifyLotteryUseCase separately checks only slice length. A record with a valid key/proof and altered payout address therefore reports verified through CLI/desktop and valid:true through REST, and ImportRecords now accepts it as cryptographically verified.

EV-150.title: Verifier checks address length but never address values
EV-150.description: At 917b8b5, internal/app/lottery/verify.go:134-140 appends VerifyWarn for a winner/address length mismatch and leaves IntegrityOK true after the switch. It never compares same-length entries. internal/app/lottery/usecase.go:225-235 only checks same winner set and equal address-slice length. internal/domain/lottery/service.go:42-47 proves every legitimate address is NameToAddress(winner), so any other value is corruption or tampering.
EV-150.source: internal/app/lottery/verify.go:134-140; internal/app/lottery/usecase.go:225-235; internal/domain/lottery/service.go:42-47; static read at commit 917b8b5

ISS-358.title: Tampered lottery winner addresses pass verification and import
ISS-358.description: A keyed draw with a valid VRF proof can change one or more WinnerAddresses without invalidating the record. VerifyRecord only warns on address-slice length mismatch and ignores values; the REST verify use case only checks length. CLI/desktop report the draw verified, REST returns valid:true, and imports preserve the tampered payout destination.

TASK-365.title: Verify winner addresses and unify all lottery integrity verdicts
TASK-365.description: Make VerifyRecord fail on winner/address length mismatch or any address that differs from NameToAddress(winner at the same index). Route VerifyLotteryUseCase through VerifyRecord so CLI, desktop, REST and import share one verdict. Add direct verifier, REST use-case, and import regressions for truncated, same-length tampered, and correctly ordered/reordered address evidence; prove them red by restoring the old length-only behavior.

DEC-039.title: Verify deterministic winner-address pairs and route every lottery verdict through VerifyRecord
DEC-039.rationale: DrawWinners derives WinnerAddresses from the ordered winner list via NameToAddress, so an address mismatch is objective corruption rather than a warning. VerifyRecord now rejects length or value mismatches while accepting consistent pair reordering. VerifyLotteryUseCase delegates to that report and exposes its first failure reason, eliminating a weaker REST-only copy that could drift from CLI, desktop and import. A valid VRF proof authenticates the winner stream, not arbitrary JSON payout destinations, so both checks are required for an honest verified verdict.
DEC-039.alternatives_rejected: Checking only slice lengths accepts same-length payout tampering. Failing every reordered array would reject lossless tooling that keeps winner/address pairs together. Keeping duplicated REST verification logic caused the observed cross-surface split and would recreate it after future verifier changes. Making address mismatch a warning would continue returning valid:true for a record with a wrong payout destination.

EV-151.title: Winner-address tampering now fails direct, REST, and import verification
EV-151.description: Commit a2a1214 makes VerifyRecord reject truncated addresses and any same-length value not equal to NameToAddress(winner at that index), while accepting consistently reordered pairs. VerifyLotteryUseCase delegates to VerifyRecord and REST returns the first failure reason. Before the code change, the new direct verifier, REST use-case, and import tests all failed: REST returned valid:true and import accepted the tampered payout address. After the change, 20 shuffled runs, focused race tests, full go test ./..., full race, coverage, just check, just desktop-check, and golangci-lint (0 issues) passed.

CHG-364.title: Verify deterministic winner-address pairs and unify lottery verdicts
CHG-364.description: VerifyRecord now fails on winner/address length or value mismatch, accepts consistent pair reordering, and VerifyLotteryUseCase delegates to it so REST, CLI, desktop, and import share one verdict. Adds direct, REST handler, use-case, and import tampering regressions and removes the now-unused warning status.

ISS-360.title: Oracle request headers cannot be set through any source creation surface
ISS-360.description: DataSource.Headers is persisted and returned by GET /api/v1/oracle/sources, and the HTTP fetcher applies it to outgoing requests, but AddSourceRequest has no Headers field and AddSourceUseCase never copies one. The REST CreateSource decoder, CLI oracle source add, web Add Source form, and oracle TUI form likewise expose no header input. Authenticated/private feeds that require Authorization or vendor API-key headers therefore cannot be configured through any public write surface despite storage/fetch support. TASK-367.title: Expose oracle request headers end-to-end across REST, CLI, web, and TUI
TASK-367.description: Add Headers to AddSourceRequest and propagate it into oracle.DataSource. Accept JSON-object headers on REST POST /api/v1/oracle/sources, CLI oracle source add --headers, the web Add Source form, and the oracle TUI form. Keep effective headers visible where source configuration is shown. ISS-390.title: A scheduler pass fetches sources serially and this was undocumented
ISS-390.description: Measured: with a 150ms source first and an instant one second, a pass takes 150ms and runs [slow fast]. The shape is deliberate but nothing said so, so a change to concurrent fetching would silently alter when a source counts as due.

ISS-391.title: A transfer-history page can be shorter than its limit while more rows exist
ISS-391.description: The reader skips rows whose amount will not parse after the SQL query, so a limit=3 page returned 2 with a third row still reachable by offset. A client treating len(page) as the end loses the remainder; the contract was undocumented.

CHG-406.title: Document and pin the scheduler's serial fetch shape

CHG-407.title: Document and pin the short-page contract

EV-184.source: EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN and timings on a 3000-row lottery table and a 2000-event aggregate
EV-184.summary: Measured: GetAll over 3000 lottery records is 1.5ms; the owner-scoped transfer predicate over 2000 events with the composite index is 0.4ms, flat across offsets 0..5000. Neither is a bottleneck, so both were left alone. Supersedes EV-183, whose fields were created from a placeholder.

DEC-042.title: A scheduler pass fetches serially, and a short transfer-history page is not the end of the data
DEC-042.rationale: Both behaviours are deliberate: serial fetching keeps the per-source backoff meaningful and avoids a burst of simultaneous upstream requests; skipping undecodable rows keeps a corrupt record from failing a whole page. Both were undocumented and untested, so either could have been changed silently. They are now pinned by tests and stated where the code decides.
alternatives_rejected: Fetch sources concurrently: changes the failure model and makes per-source backoff meaningless
Fail the whole page on one undecodable row: one corrupt record would hide all healthy history

ISS-392.title: Desktop pages blanked the rows they had already loaded on a refresh failure
ISS-392.description: Voting did not render loadErr at all, and the other pages returned on the error line alone, so a transient read failure hid content the loaders had kept. The renderer now keeps the last successful rows, labels them stale, and shows failures instead of empty-state notes.

ISS-393.title: Lottery history ordered same-second draws by insertion order

The order is timestamp DESC, block_height DESC, id, backed by idx_lottery_recency (migration 000007).

ISS-421.title: The oracle dial guard could be routed around through a NAT64 prefix
ISS-421.description: On an IPv6-only network [64:ff9b::7f00:1] translates to 127.0.0.1 at the network edge; the block list only knew IPv4 loopback and IPv6 ULA/link-local, so an IPv6 literal could reach loopback. Both NAT64 prefixes plus multicast, reserved, benchmark, documentation and discard-only ranges are refused; TestBlockedIPRanges pins them.

ISS-434.title: The desktop Oracle feed-health read swallowed its error

ISS-435.title: The desktop Oracle add form swallowed preset-load failures
